name: netris
why: Networked Tetris played over a socket, an old-school multiplayer terminal game with some charm.

brief.what_it_is: Netris is a free, networked variant of Tetris that runs as a text-based program in the terminal, using ncurses. Two players can play against each other over a network. When one player clears two or three lines with a single piece, the opponent gets one or two unfilled lines at the bottom of their screen. Clearing four lines at once sends four. The package page does not say what the program takes in or puts out beyond the game itself. The scout note describes it as playing over a socket, but the page does not state that.
brief.why_it_exists: The page gives no explicit motivation. The only framing from the author is that the one-player mode is "a tad boring at the moment" and that the author plans to fix that later.
brief.how_it_works: The page describes the head-to-head rule: lines cleared with one piece push garbage lines onto the opponent's board. It also says the version "at least partially supports robots", with a protocol described in the documentation and a sample robot in the examples. The page does not explain the network transport or how the protocol works in detail.
brief.install_notes: The homepage is Debian's package page, not the upstream project, so the install route it documents is Debian packages (sid, forky, bookworm, bullseye). The package is version 0.52-12 and is available for many architectures, including amd64, arm64, armhf, i386, ppc64el, riscv64 and s390x, plus several unofficial ports. Runtime dependencies are libc6 (>= 2.34) and libncurses6 / libtinfo6. No accounts, configuration or first-run steps are mentioned. The brew formula's caveats field is empty. I did not see a brew-specific install note.
brief.standout: It is an old-school two-player terminal Tetris where clearing lines sends garbage rows to the opponent, and it has a documented robot protocol with a sample bot. The robot hook is the more unusual part for a game of this kind.
brief.status: Packaged and maintained within Debian by the Debian Games Team (with Rhonda D'Vine listed as a co-maintainer), shown in the unstable, testing and stable suites. The page gives no upstream release date or last commit, so upstream activity is unknown. The Debian package is current enough to show up in sid.
brief.caveats: The page is a Debian package listing, not the author's own homepage or README, so the upstream project's own description and docs were not reached. The author says single-player mode never speeds up and has no scoring. Robot support is only partial. The page does not mention Windows or macOS, and the brew formula's install notes are empty. The page lists no licence beyond a link to the copyright file, which I did not open.
quotes: Netris is a free, networked variant of Tetris.
One-player mode is a tad boring at the moment because it never gets any faster and there's no scoring.
This version at least partially supports robots. You can find the protocol description in the documentation and a sample robot in the examples.
